scope: Independent read-only input/helper and official-manual review; no runtime operations or native disassembly
status: Prior long-LOAD attempts did not exercise the documented Instant Doubles gesture; documented UI flow remains untested

official_sources.fact: Double-press LOAD on the destination deck, or hold its BEAT SYNC(INST.DOUBLES) button. It copies the active opposite-side local deck, or a connected PRO DJ LINK sync master, at the same playback position. A held LOAD is not the documented gesture.

Load Lock can prevent loading another track onto a playing destination. No separate Instant Doubles enable/disable item is listed here; that does not establish every exact-firmware eligibility predicate.

local_helper_findings.fact: The corrected attempt holds destination LOAD for1.5 host seconds using az-drive._hold. It generates sustained press/release, not two distinct LOAD presses.

LOAD uses mixer bus2, byte33: deck1 mask0x08, deck2 mask0x04. _mixer preserves mixer state and browse knob counter. _hold repeats pressed frames then releases; load() sends one pressed frame then sleeps and releases. Separate host SSH sends can distort timing. SYNC2 uses ERP bus0 byte0x10 mask0x02.

Existing hold_erp schedules repeated pressed/released phases in a single guest command using guest uptime, avoiding per-frame SSH timing. Its supported load action currently accepts only a short press. This review does not modify or execute the helper.

smallest_next_owner_UI_control: Use a healthy-controller fixture with one verified native USB track playing on active deck1; no simulated external peer. Pause/unload target deck2 through native UI so target playback/Load Lock cannot obscure the result.

Verify ordinary single LOAD2 from a populated, focused native track list issues a successful normal load, then unload target2 again. This controls mixer input delivery and track eligibility without invoking the diagnostic API.

Send two destination LOAD2 down/up edges with repeated native frames and a final release, timed in one guest connection. An initial100ms down/100ms up/100ms down/release sequence is an exploratory timing choice, not a proven firmware threshold. Preserve existing mixer levels and knob counter.

Require destination title/content to match the source, position close to the source and native successful completion; a no-op requires checking actual delivered edges/timing before declaring the feature unavailable.

If double-LOAD remains inconclusive, independently try the documented hold-SYNC2 alternative using repeated ERP frames for an exploratory1.5s and a final release. Record any normal sync toggle separately from a successful duplicate.
After a native-source user-flow control succeeds, repeat the same verified gesture on a healthy mounted private source. Only then use it for stale-request/reconnect acceptance.
unproven: Exact firmware double-click window and hold threshold
Exact native source/target eligibility predicates and any additional feature configuration

conclusion: Do not describe Instant Doubles as broken from the long-LOAD no-op. The documented gesture has not yet been exercised in the frozen supported-artifact evidence.
